From e2bb9fab08cbcc7922050c7eb0bd650807abfa4e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2021 08:32:38 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix invalid unit check

The uncore unit with the type ID 0 and the unit ID 0 is missed.

The table3 of the uncore unit maybe 0. The
uncore_discovery_invalid_unit() mistakenly treated it as an invalid
value.

Remove the !unit.table3 check.

Fixes: edae1f06c2cd ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: Parse uncore discovery tables")
Signed-off-by: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1629991963-102621-3-git-send-email-kan.liang@linux.intel.com

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
index 7280c8a3c831..6d735611c281 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
+++ b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
@@ -30,7 +30,7 @@
 
 
 #define uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)			\
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	\
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
 	 unit.table1 == -1ULL || unit.ctl == -1ULL ||	\
 	 unit.table3 == -1ULL)
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h`**
   - The macro `uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)` was modified by removing the check for `unit.table3`. The original condition checked if `unit.table3` was not present or equal to `-1ULL`, which was deemed incorrect for the case where both type ID and unit ID are 0. The updated condition now only checks for `unit.table1`, `unit.ctl`, and their respective invalid values.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of uncore units with type ID 0 and unit ID 0. By removing the check for `unit.table3`, the patch ensures that valid uncore units are not incorrectly marked as invalid, thus improving the accuracy of the uncore discovery process. This change is a fix for the previously introduced logic in commit `edae1f06c2cd`, which incorrectly treated certain valid configurations as invalid.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the `unit.table3` value in the `uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)` macro. The logic mistakenly treated a valid uncore unit (with type ID 0 and unit ID 0) as invalid when `unit.table3` was 0, leading to false negatives in uncore unit discovery. The check for `unit.table3` was unnecessary and incorrect, as it could be a valid value in certain cases.

Here is the patch:
 
 #define uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)			\
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	\
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
 	 unit.table1 == -1ULL || unit.ctl == -1ULL ||	\
 	 unit.table3 == -1ULL)

The check for `unit.table3` being 0 was incorrectly treating a valid uncore unit (with type ID 0 and unit ID 0) as invalid. This led to false negatives in the uncore unit discovery process, as the logic mistakenly excluded valid units based on the value of `unit.table3`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
```
Reason:
By removing the check for `unit.table3`, the code now correctly allows for the possibility that `unit.table3` can be 0, which is a valid state for certain uncore units. This change ensures that valid uncore units are not incorrectly marked as invalid, thus fixing the bug in the uncore unit discovery logic.
